stage1.impression: A witty, well-composed set-up: low window sun throws the gable-top speaker's carton silhouette into a warm patch on a dark navy wainscot, and the red-and-white product reads instantly. But the product is the least convincing thing in the frame: its white front and the sliver of sunlit side read as one flat, slightly grey value with no sun modelling to match the crisp shadow it casts, while the streaky tan patch, the murky floor and the near-black right third keep it a good draft rather than a homepage hero.

blocking_9: The product carries the sun: side-right 226-238 and at least 40% of the product's width, the front 35-60 levels below it with at least 25 levels of fall-off from under the gable to above the plinth (now: side 37 px wide at 218.2, front 205-219, front/side corner step 17).

The carton silhouette reads at a glance: flanks no wider than 6 px, core at most 34, eave corners level within 10 px, fin chimney visible, at least 60 px clear of the product and inside the patch with at least 0.1 m to spare.

The patch reads as low sun on painted panelling: median 145-175, warm (R minus B at least 70), relief range 4.5-7 levels with no vertical veneer streaks, soft (about 20 px) window edges against the crisp silhouette flanks.

No dead near-black field: the wall left of the patch and right of the product each at most 20% of the width with median at least 30 and visible panelling; plaster band above the rail at most 12% of the height (now right third 30.8, top band 26.8, upper right wall 18.7).

The floor grounds the product: sunlit band at least 65 with the product's shadow running unbroken from its base to the wall silhouette, and the shaded lower-left floor at least 35 with readable planks (now 28.3).
The white reads as clear-coated lacquer: a soft, motivated reflection gradient of at least 8 levels on the shaded front or the roof that does not lift the front out of its band.
The sunlit accent holds to the swatch: side-right plinth and gable triangle within dE2000 5 of #C62828 (side-right plinth now 13.0, RGB 243/76/60).
The drivers read as the named products: black anodised woofer and papyrus mid with soft motivated highlights, no stray hot spot and no dead-black disc (mid-cone median now 6.4).

changes.problem: The frontsheen panel fakes the front's gradient; from the new view the front still mirrors it (about 12 deg off its mirror direction), which would add an unmotivated sheen of about +0.2 linear and flatten the shade face again.

changes.expected: Streak range held at 5-7 levels in the patch: brushed paint, not grain. This continues round 14's cut (0.66 to 0.51), scaled for the stronger, more raking sun, rather than reversing it; the lower bound keeps enough texture that the patch does not go back to flat beige (round 12).

changes.problem: The glints are pinned to the woofer's old surface points; with the product moved 0.25 m and re-lit from camera-left they would land as stray highlights at arbitrary spots (round 13's odd bent white highlight).

changes.expected: No glint lamps (equivalent to glints.1 and glints.2 power_w 0): the woofer reads by the fill's soft reflection on its upper left and the raking sun on its trim ring, with no isolated hot spot on the cap.

out_of_scope.request: Reshape the tweeter waveguide (shallower bowl, softer rim) so it reads less like an eye in the roof slope
out_of_scope.why: Its depth, profile and mouth are set by acoustic simulation and are fixed; only light and camera may change how it reads, which c1, c2 and c4 do by putting a raking sun and the camera-left fill across that slope.

out_of_scope.request: Hide the grey outer lip of the woofer trim ring on the driver's left
out_of_scope.why: The drivers are real products mounted flush under trim rings by the owner's decision; their geometry, materials and colours are fixed.
